findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_board.py claim_eligibility (~l.237-240) drops `stale-heartbeat` for handed-off items. `doctor` therefore reports nothing for them. `--fix` removes only terminal problems (merged PR, missing worktree). The scope gate refusal at ~l.286-290 tells the operator to run `agent_board.py finish` by hand. The same sibling-overlap blind spot is already noted in design.md Risks.
findings.summary: A handed-off board record whose PR is closed without merging, or abandoned, is never reclaimed automatically. It stays on the board indefinitely.

findings.evidence: agent_board.py ~l.323-324 calls `queue._latest`, `queue._comments`, `queue._repo` and `queue._is_ancestor`. The test (tests/test_rehandoff_board.py RehandoffAcceptanceTests.refusal) patches those same private names, so any rename in publication_queue breaks both the code and the tests together. A public wrapper in publication_queue would make the contract explicit.
findings.summary: agent_board.rehandoff_refusal calls underscore-private helpers of publication_queue and adds network and `gh` calls to a previously local, read-only scope gate. This couples two modules through private APIs.
